sections.html:
Laclede County is a rural Ozarks county in south central Missouri. Lebanon holds the courthouse and is the only big city, and a stretch of the Mark Twain National Forest lies inside the county line. Smaller incorporated places include Conway, Richland, Phillipsburg, Stoutland and Evergreen. Population was 36,943 in July 2025.

The median owner-occupied home is worth $168,400, and 68.2% of homes are lived in by their owners, out of 16,211 housing units. Figure out whether your house is within a city limit or out on a county road before listing, because that changes the levies on your bill. Five public school districts have campuses here. The one serving your address adds its own levy, so tell buyers which it is.

A paid-off house has no escrow account to pay for you. The statement from the collector is your only reminder, so an heir to a house with no loan should mark the due date on a calendar.

Worth is the Assessor's call; billing is the Collector of Revenue's. The collector's office works strictly from the assessor's records and has no power to change a bill. Mistakes in acreage, owner name or parcel description therefore go to the Assessor at (417) 532-7163.

The Collector also handles merchant license fees and railroad and utility tax, and distributes money to schools, road districts, fire protection entities and other local subdivisions. Mortgage companies send escrow payments to the same counter.

The collector's website finds a bill by owner name, parcel number, street address or account number, and shows payment history. Pull up your parcel ahead of listing to see which years are settled.

sections.h2: When bills arrive and how to pay
sections.html:
Once the County Clerk hands over the tax books in late October, the office starts printing, and statements go out in November. The due date is December 31. You get one statement for real estate and another for personal property, and a single check can pay both.

Counter hours are 8am to 4pm, Monday through Friday, except state and federal holidays. For payments after December 31, the delinquency schedule on your statement applies, and the office will quote the penalty on request.

  • At the counter: cash, personal check, money order or cashier's check.
  • By mail: a check in the return envelope, and never cash.
  • By card, on the website or over the phone, plus a convenience fee.
  • In the drop box at the Second Street courthouse entrance, usable at any hour.

Your paid receipt returns by mail after processing. A late payment left in the drop box without its penalty is sent back.

In a typical year, the dates run like this.

A year of Laclede County property tax dates
WhenWhat happens
Late OctoberStatements are printed once the tax books arrive
NovemberReal estate and personal property statements go out
April 1 to the last Friday in MayRenewal period for the senior tax credit
Second Monday in JulyLast day to appeal a value to the county board
Fourth Monday in August, 10 a.m.Delinquent tax certificate sale at the courthouse
December 31Bill due

Spreading the bill out is possible for most owners. Under the Collector's prepay plan you make ten equal payments based on last year's tax, an eleventh payment settles whatever is left, and the money comes out of your bank account automatically. A delinquent account or a parcel paid through lender escrow is not eligible. The sign-up number is (417) 532-4301.

The senior credit is a different tool. It holds the homestead real estate tax at its first-year level. One home only, and you must live there. Renewal comes yearly, from April 1 through the last Friday in May. Year one always shows a zero credit since earlier years are never refunded. The Collector can say when the next application period starts.

Because it freezes the tax rather than removing it, the tax stays on the home. A seller already enrolled should ask what becomes of the credit at a change of ownership.

sections.h2: What if my value is too high?
sections.html:
The order is Assessor, then the county board of equalization, then the State Tax Commission. Your appeal must reach the board by the second Monday in July. The board's letter starts a 30-day clock for going to the Commission.

Disputing a value does not put you behind on the bill. If you protest, the Commission's guidance is to mail the entire payment to the collector, label it a protest and enclose your written reasons and the market value you claim. A postmark on or before December 31 counts.

Estates, trusts, LLCs and corporations cannot file with the Commission without a lawyer, which is worth remembering for anyone settling a relative's estate ahead of a sale.

In August a bidder may pay your delinquent tax and walk away with a certificate of purchase instead of a deed. It happens on the fourth Monday at 10 a.m., at the courthouse, 200 N. Adams in Lebanon, following three weeks of newspaper notice. If you pay the taxes, penalty, interest and costs before the bidding starts, the parcel comes off the list.

To redeem after a sale, the owner pays the certificate's base amount plus 10% annual interest, along with any later tax the buyer paid, at the same interest. The Collector asks for a day's notice and suggests allowing 20 minutes.

When the year is up, the holder may seek a collector's deed, but only after certified-mail notices go to the owner and lienholders at least 90 days earlier. Liens survive the sale itself. Bid money above the taxes and costs belongs to the owner of record.

Owing tax does not rule out a closing; the sale price pays it off. Three steps get it done.

  1. Get an exact payoff from the collector.
  2. Pass that number to the title company.
  3. Have the closing pay the collector from the price.

A few cases need extra care.

  • If you bought the house before October, the statement may have gone to the previous owner, so ask them and the collector.
  • If the August sale is close, pay the balance before that date.
  • Tell the collector about the sale if you use the installment plan or the senior credit.
  • Call the Assessor about a wrong value well before July.

Written payoff figures protect you if the amount shifts before the closing date. With a cash buyer there is no lender sign-off to wait for, so the title company can pay the collector as soon as it has the number.

faqs.q: Is the Laclede County property tax deadline December 31?
faqs.a: Yes. Statements arrive in November and are due December 31. Payment after that date follows the delinquency schedule on the statement.

faqs.q: Which office fixes an error in my Laclede County parcel record?
faqs.a: The Assessor, at (417) 532-7163. The collector cannot change a bill, since it must collect from the assessor's records.

faqs.q: Can I pay Laclede County property tax by card?
faqs.a: Yes. Cards work online or by phone, with a convenience fee. The office also takes cash, checks and money orders, and a courthouse drop box is open all day.

faqs.q: When must I appeal a Laclede County value?
faqs.a: The county board of equalization needs your appeal by the second Monday in July. The State Tax Commission allows 30 days from the date of the board's letter.

faqs.q: Is it possible to close on a Laclede County home with back tax owed?
faqs.a: Yes. Get a written payoff from the collector so the title company can pay it from your proceeds. If the August sale is near, clearing the balance first keeps the parcel off the list.
